tasks.intro: Four independent hypothetical oil wells with two daily rate snapshots each. These are not a field forecast; all rates are STB/D.
tasks.goal: For each well calculate percentage decline from initial to final rate. Report all four declines, mean, maximum, minimum, range, the largest-decline well and descending ranking. Also report combined initial and final daily rates and the fleet-weighted percentage decline. Do not confuse fleet-weighted decline with unweighted mean.

tasks.intro: Four independent hypothetical RFT pressure-gauge QC pairs; reference and observed pressures are in psi. This is instrument-error arithmetic, not a flow-regime diagnosis.
tasks.goal: Compute signed gauge error observed minus reference and absolute error for A-D. Report all eight values, mean signed bias, mean absolute error, root-mean-square error, maximum absolute error, the worst gauge and descending ranking by absolute error. Do not claim these synthetic QC readings prove reservoir properties.

tasks.intro: Four separate hypothetical radial-drainage geometries; each re and rw is a radius in ft.
tasks.goal: Locate the KB dimensionless external-radius definition reD=re/rw. Calculate reD for A-D, mean, maximum, minimum, range, largest-reD geometry and descending ranking. Treat these as geometric ratios, not a full well-test solution.

tasks.intro: Four separate hypothetical 10 cc RFT probe-chamber drawdowns; T2 values below are elapsed seconds, not hours. The source relation is specific to this 10 cc probe example.
tasks.goal: Use the KB probe relation q2=10/T2 and compute illustrative probe flow rates q2 for A-D in cc/s. Report mean, maximum, minimum, range, highest-flow case and descending ranking. Do not generalize the 10 cc numerator to a different chamber or infer permeability without other required inputs.

tasks.intro: Four independent hypothetical NMR logs; MPHI is effective porosity and MCBW is clay-bound-water porosity, both expressed in percent of bulk rock.
tasks.goal: Use the KB NMR relation MSIG=MPHI+MCBW to compute total NMR porosity MSIG for A-D in percent. Report mean, maximum, minimum, range, top case and descending ranking. Do not call MPHI alone total porosity.

tasks.intro: Four hypothetical gas-core permeability corrections. kg is apparent gas permeability in mD; b and mean flowing p are both in psi. The Klinkenberg relation is in a separate handbook chapter.
tasks.goal: Find the KB Klinkenberg correction kL=kg/(1+b/p), then calculate liquid-equivalent permeability kL for A-D in mD. Report mean, maximum, minimum, range, highest case and descending ranking. Keep gas and corrected liquid permeabilities distinct.

tasks.intro: Compare the drainage-radius geometries stated in two separate C13 and C14 textbook exercises. They describe different hypothetical developments, not the same reservoir.
tasks.goal: Retrieve the C13 and C14 radii from two KB exercise passages and the separate definition reD=re/rw. Compute reD for each exercise, mean, maximum, minimum, range, the larger-ratio exercise, descending ranking and C13/C14 ratio. Keep the two exercises' input provenance separate; do not infer productivity index.

tasks.intro: Three Layer 1-3 permeability/thickness pairs in one well-test exercise and a fourth pair in a separate exercise. D must not be called a fourth layer of the first reservoir.
tasks.goal: Retrieve the separately labelled k and h values and compute each illustrative permeability-thickness product k times h (mD-ft) for A=Layer 1, B=Layer 2, C=Layer 3, D=the separate 3.5 exercise. Report all four products, mean, maximum, minimum, range, top case and descending ranking. A product is only a comparison proxy, not a productivity index.

tasks.intro: One hypothetical pressure-drawdown check, both pressures in psi.
tasks.goal: Report pressure drawdown initial minus flowing in psi. Direct subtraction is sufficient; Python is optional. Do not infer permeability.

tasks.intro: A textbook density-neutron crossplot example reports a porosity. The target below is a hypothetical comparison threshold, not the source's target.
tasks.goal: Retrieve the example's 18% porosity and report how many percentage points it lies below the hypothetical 20% target. One subtraction is enough; Python is optional. Do not call this a field porosity deficit.

tasks.intro: Conceptual WFT monitoring question only; no numeric inputs or calculation request.
tasks.goal: Explain why fault-block crossflow cannot be inferred reliably from a distributed pressure survey alone when rate allocation and drained pore volumes are unknown. Cite the KB discussion and describe missing measurements; do not calculate.

tasks.intro: Conceptual dual-water petrophysics question only; no arithmetic request.
tasks.goal: Explain the distinction between total pore-volume water and bound/connate water in a shaly-sand interpretation and why bound water complicates a simple resistivity reading. Cite the handbook discussion; do not calculate.
